A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLV research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on six benchmarks, ablations, training dynamics, and analyses of generated reasoning and data validation.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, a cold-start ablation, formalization comparisons, intermediate-step analysis, and LegalBench-SARA results.

M1.justification: The proposed synthesis pipeline, SFT objective, hierarchical rewards, GRPO optimization, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 5.4 explicitly clarifies that flexible verification uses the existing inference loop. FLV-ZeroRL is an added ablation, not a replacement method.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds LegalBench-SARA entailment evaluation, testing multi-step reasoning over US tax statutes. This is a focused extension of evaluation coverage; the original six benchmarks, training sources, and represented training categories remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CoRT-1.5B-RL, explicitly identifying its DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B backbone. Table 2 adds FLV-ZeroRL, and Table 9 compares DeepSeek-V3.2 and Qwen3-235B with Claude Sonnet 4.5 for formalization. Existing comparators are retained; the LegalBench evaluation uses previously evaluated baseline methods.

E3.justification: Added experimental designs include RL without SFT initialization, conversion evaluation on 103 traces per formalizer, and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct classification of execution logs at rollout steps 20, 40, and 60. Existing training budgets, decoding procedures, and primary benchmark settings remain unchanged. Newly documented filtering details do not establish that the original training data changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive analyses addressing three previously untested questions: the contribution of SFT initialization, intermediate-step satisfiability during RL, and sensitivity of formalization success to the synthesis model. These appear in Section 5.3 and Appendices G–H. The existing verification-paradigm, package-usage, efficiency, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: AIME24 still reports avg@16, and the existing distribution summaries are retained. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 103-trace comparison adds a sample size, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark table entries are unchanged, but v2 adds several distinct result sets: CoRT-1.5B-RL averages 37.7, FLV-ZeroRL averages 42.7, and FLV-RL scores 64.7 on LegalBench-SARA. Tables 4, 8, and 9 add filtering yields, SAT proportions of 14.7%, 16.9%, and 17.0%, and formalization success comparisons. These are additional findings, not improvements from rerunning retained settings. The new cold-start paragraph gives the base average as 30.3, inconsistent with Table 2's retained 30.0.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20, the reward-computation complexity argument, and the economic-case derivations are retained. Appendix G adds informal conceptual interpretation rather than new mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about interleaved verification, two-stage training, cross-domain reasoning, and headline margins of 10.4% and 14.2%. Added experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the cold-start ablation as evidence of newly learned verification skills and rising SAT proportions as evidence of hallucination reduction. Appendix H adds arguments about synthesis-model costs and reproducibility. The limitations now identify General-Reasoner specifically as the comparator for approximately doubled RL training time; the existing formalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future release promise with a stated model-and-dataset location on Hugging Face. Appendix B newly documents filtering and deduplication, including 84,641 generated chains, 19,543 filtered samples, and 14,117 final samples. New analyses identify their formalization models and log classifier. Existing hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, reward pseudocode, and prompts remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including DeepSeekMath, LegalBench, LegalReasoner, and work on planning, process rewards, and model merging. The positioning against post-hoc verification and domain-specific approaches remains substantially unchanged. CoRT was already cited in v1; its new experimental participation is distinct from a citation addition.

P1.justification: v2 adds the cold-start discussion, filtering explanation, Appendices G–I, and acknowledgements, while making localized clarification and author/publication-information edits. Former Appendices G–I become J–L. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Four compact tables are added: v2 Tables 4 and 8–10. Tables 1–2 gain rows, and Table 1 gains a backbone footnote. Existing figures and tables are relocated or renumbered as content reflows; the nine original figures and overall document design remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The cold-start control, legal-entailment evaluation, and formalization comparison provide useful additional empirical support, while filtering details and the reported model/data location improve reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited by the new base-score inconsistency and by interpreting model-classified SAT rates as stronger evidence of hallucination reduction than the diagnostic establishes. Overall, v2 offers a modest improvement without resolving the paper's broader soundness claims.
